additions.name: iTech Tower 3.1 — remaining development and fit-out

status.summary: iTech Tower 3.1 is a commercial data centre at 3 On Kui Street in Fanling. Its first two phases were delivered to Amazon Data Services Hong Kong Limited in December 2025 and generate rental income. Grand Ming reported continuing development and fit-out work on 18 September 2026. The proposed sale to Amazon remains conditional.

locator.precision: Centroid of Fanling Sheung Shui Town Lot No. 289, a 1662 m² property at 3 On Kui Street, On Lok Tsuen, Fanling. This is a lot-level marker, not a surveyed building outline, entrance or individual data hall.
locator.identity_review: Grand Ming's 18 September 2026 filing identifies Property 1 at 3 On Kui Street, Fanling. LandsD's Land Exchange Transactions dataset gives that exact numbered address for FSSTL 289; CSDI maps it to a single LotCSUID 500000289 polygon. The transaction map's reference point falls inside the polygon. No adjacent property's address or geocoder fallback is used.
locator.uncertainty_reason: LandsD provides no positional tolerance for the lot boundary. The polygon spans about 60.0 by 58.7 m; agreement between two government coordinate-transform outputs does not establish survey accuracy.

additions.distinctness_review: Checked all 653 sites, 695 projects, 3558 evidence rows, original source records, identity mappings and tracked holds in the sixtyfirst dataset for iTech, Grand Ming, Regal Development, Golden Ford, On Kui, On Chuen and Chinese aliases. No match; the iTech substring in titech.ac.jp is unrelated. Nearest admitted site is Sandy Ridge, more than 4.5 km away. Properties 1 and 2 are designed to operate together but have separate numbered addresses, separate legal lots and a 90.33 m gap between their official lot polygons. They are distinct noncontiguous properties, each with its own facility and agreement, and are admitted as two physical sites. SUNeVision MEGA Fanling at 11 On Chuen Street and Vantage at 3 On Chuen Street are different properties.
additions.successor_review: The 30 September circular postponement and issuer announcement index captured 25 October contain no later construction observation or completed sale. The circular target is 26 October, after this review. Keep 18 September as the construction observation; February 26, 2027 is a conditional transaction-closing target, not a facility-completion target.

additions.name: (仮称)有明TK2データセンター — planned data-centre building

status.summary: Ariake TK2 is a planned data centre on a shared development property in Koto, Tokyo. A notification received by the Tokyo Metropolitan Government on 7 September 2026 lists 32,972.49 m² of gross floor area and a height of 59.98 m for the data-centre building. Construction is scheduled to begin on 1 March 2027; this is a forecast. The separate hotel on the property is excluded from this Atlas project.

locator.precision: Exact GSI residential-address feature for 有明3-5-1, near the southern street edge of the shared Ariake TK2 / hotel development property. It is a labelled parent-property address marker; it does not locate the northern data-centre building, any footprint, legal lot boundary, entrance or active construction extent. The adjacent hotel is not an Atlas project.
locator.identity_review: Tokyo notification 31 (7 September 2026) names the data-centre/hotel plan on 有明二丁目1-65, 67, 69, 75 and 三丁目1-24. The primary developer notice reproduced in a June 2026 site photograph prints the identical five lots and gives 住居表示 東京都江東区有明3-5-1. GSI returns exactly that full residential address, without fallback to the ward, chome or block. GSI standard map and seamless imagery confirm the point is at the southern street edge of the shared parent property, which matches the distinctive curved road and station-side public plaza in the developer diagram. This corroborates identity, not current works. Source-photo provenance remains explicit.
locator.uncertainty_reason: The GSI address-search response does not publish positional accuracy or survey metadata. The point represents the shared development address and lies near its southern edge, offset from the proposed northern data-centre block by an unmeasured distance. Six decimal places are source precision, not surveyed accuracy.

additions.distinctness_review: Screened against all current sites/projects of verified_construction_core/2026-10-23-research-sixtyfirst for Ariake, TK2, Aran and 有明 and by distance. No existing site or project matches. Nearest current site is Koto Sengoku 3-chome Data Centre ((仮称)江東区千石三丁目計画) (5.56 km away); its Sengoku lots are different. This resolves the Ariake geometry hold in research-countries-2026-10-23-fiftyfifth-holds.json. NEXTDC TK1/TK2, Shiohama Phase II and the adjacent Ariake Hotel are separate and are not merged or admitted here. No operator inferred from the TK2 code.
additions.successor_review: Re-read Tokyo April–September notification CSV on 25 October 2026; exact bytes match the 23 October capture. It records September notification and a future March 2027 construction start. Discovery-only October architecture updates still describe the future start and do not establish a primary later physical milestone. No achieved start, building permission, completion or operation was found. Retain announced as of the explicit notification date, 7 September 2026.

status.summary: The Hong Kong government confirmed on 21 October 2026 that construction of the Sandy Ridge Data Facility Cluster had begun. The development remains under construction; the government’s computing-capacity target for 2032 is prospective.

status_updates.identity_review: The government report names the same Sandy Ridge Data Facility Cluster already tied to D.D. 89 Lot 953 by the 2 March 2026 tender result. Preserve the existing site, project, official lot polygon, roles and earlier evidence.
status_updates.successor_review: Independent government-source searches through 25 October found the 21 October report as the newest authoritative physical-status observation. The 14 October LegCo report is its predecessor. Neither the first-phase 2027 forecast nor the projected 2032 computing target establishes operation.
